text: This slice is the rwb-payment half of the legacy key: it resolves the PAYMENT_MATCH version in force from the registry of rwb-decision, fetches the model of that version, evaluates it in this service through the embedded Drools kit in row order, writes the match as a local decision record in the same transaction as the proceeds row, and publishes the events; the registry, its load checks, its four-eyes approval, its 00:01 promotion and its rollback stay with rwb-decision (RWB-P7-E2027-APP), the workbook with rwb-case (RWB-P3-E2042-APP), the session and rights with rwb-access, and the installment shortfall with rwb-treatment. Legacy AC6 is read through the rwb-decision contract mock, keeping every legacy step and value.
why: The Work Package fixes this story in rwb-payment with DP-04 and lists AC6 among its criteria, but AC6 loads and checks a package in another service; DP-04 keeps the registry central in rwb-decision and the evaluation local in the owning service, so the load is mocked here and the evaluation is proved here.
read: Work Package B2-P8-002 story line RWB-P8-E2027-APP (patterns DP04, acs AC6, AC7, AC10, C row without RWB-P7-E1073-CON); Template and Rules v1 R5.4 and R5.5 DP-04; RWB-E2-027 sections 4, 7 and 12; P8 context pack service row.
confirm: Solution architect with the owners of rwb-decision and rwb-case
impact: Medium: the boundary is written once, so a later move of the load or the evaluation changes one service and no business value and no legacy value.
